title: Runbook Fabricator: Admin Sidecar & Task Fan-out Engine
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Prototype and deliver an agent-sidecar and orchestration layer that compiles operator runbooks into replayable, idempotent task graphs which can be executed, dry-run, or simulated by the support surface. The Fabricator will support fan-out to short-lived worker lambdas, safe retries, permission checks, and structured audit events so SREs and support engineers can run deterministic remediation without SSHing to hosts.
acceptance_criteria: Runbooks can be authored in YAML/Markdown and compiled to a task graph via the fabricator CLI or Console UI.
Each compiled task emits structured audit events (actor, trace, inputs, outputs, success/failure) to the audit-log stream.
Task execution supports dry-run and simulated execution modes with side effects suppressed.
Idempotency guarantees: re-run of any completed step within the same trace is a no-op and logged.
Integration test harness with synthetic clusters demonstrates at least 3 example runbooks (DB failover, cache flush, model reload) end-to-end.
Canary rollout to staging + 10% of Dedicated instances with automated rollback on error-rate spike.
RBAC checks enforced: only users in Ops role can execute destructive steps; read-only staff can run dry-run.
Telemetry: success rate, median time to remediation, tokens consumed, and audit latency are visible in the Ops Console dashboard.
PR with implementation and unit+integration tests merged into main and referenced in ticket.
proposed_solution: Implement a small Go-based admin sidecar that exposes an RPC/API to accept a compiled runbook task graph. The sidecar will validate steps, map step types to handlers (shell, kubectl, http-call, redwood-api), and delegate execution to a local sandbox or a worker pool. Use a deterministic trace ID for idempotency with a lightweight key-value transaction log. Fan-out tasks use the existing agentlet invocation endpoint; fallback to local execution when worker pool is disabled. Audit events are written to the event-collector topic with a compact structured schema (actor, action, step_id, status, hash).
implementation_notes: Sidecar language: Go (reuse existing agentlet client libraries).
Task graph format: convert existing runbook DSL to protobuf-lite representation for compactness and versioning.
Idempotency store: use Postgres with advisory locks for quick wins; evaluate RocksDB local store for extreme latency cases.
Safety gate: destructive steps must include 'safety_token' confirmed via Console or 2FA for manual runs.
Observability: instrument with OpenTelemetry spans, attach trace-id to audit events, and push metrics to metrics-ingest.
Failure modes: transient errors -> exponential backoff & retry up to configured attempts; persistent failure -> mark trace failed and surface rollback suggestions in UI.
Backward compatibility: support older runbook YAML v1 and new v2 with a compatibility layer.
Testing: include a unit test harness that can stub handlers and a networked integration test running against minikube and a Postgres test instance.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal engineering team opt-in on dedicated dev stack (1 week)
Beta: staged rollout to staging infra + smoke tests (2 weeks)
Canary: enable on 10% Dedicated pool with feature flag monitor for 48h
Full: enable on all Dedicated and Hosted admin-sidecars with ops training and updated runbook library
testing_plan: Unit tests for compiler, handlers, and idempotency store
Integration tests: 3 example runbooks against staging cluster
Chaos tests: inject worker failures and network partitions to validate retries and rollback
Security tests: RBAC role matrix verification and audit trail tamper-checks
blockers: Agentlet auth token exchange (blocked on ENG-672401 token refresh changes)
Decision on durable local store (Postgres vs RocksDB) pending infra budget approval
Security review scheduling: awaiting SecOps signoff window
